prompt: Draw the entire Taipei 101, from its base to the tip of its spire, as a highly detailed, realistic architectural illustration using editable 2D shapes. Use a fixed elevated three-quarter view looking down at the building, with clearly visible top surfaces and consistent perspective. Preserve its distinctive silhouette, projecting bamboo-shaped tiers, façade structure, window frames, and visible ornamentation. Render realistic materials, lighting, and shadows. Include these details in the finished drawing without simplifying the building into broad shapes or a schematic. Draw the surfaces visible from the chosen viewpoint. Use real-world dimensions at 1 cm = 1 px before applying perspective; projected lengths should reflect the viewing angle. Use the attached aerial image only for broad massing, visible base relationships and silhouette; it is low resolution and includes temporary construction equipment that must not be drawn. Use the ornament close-up only for ornament shape/material. The images do not establish precise unseen geometry. Do not search for other reference images.
criteria: Recognizable full tower with eight tier units and crown/spire
Consistent projected edge families and alignment
Visible foreground podium relationships retained instead of a generic plinth
Coherent face lighting and material cues without unsupported detail claims
commonInstruction: Knowledge is optional reference material available through discover_knowledge and read_knowledge.
